q.t: Which fraction is equal to 1/2?
q.e: Cut each half into 2 pieces: 1 half becomes 2 quarters, so 1/2 = 2/4.

q.t: Which is bigger: 2/5 or 4/5 of the same cake?
q.e: Same bottom number means same-size pieces, so 4 pieces beat 2 pieces.

q.t: Which is bigger: 1/3 or 1/4 of the same cake?
q.e: Cutting into 3 gives bigger pieces than cutting into 4.

q.t: How many halves make one whole?
q.e: A whole cut into 2 equal parts gives 2 halves.
The bottom was multiplied by 2 (3 → 6), so the top must be too: 1 × 2 = 2.

q.t: Maa takes 5 pieces, each 1/2 of a paratha. How many parathas is that?
q.e: 2 halves make 1 whole, so 5 halves = 2 wholes and 1 half left over.

q.t: How many quarters are there in 2 wholes?
q.e: Each whole has 4 quarters, so 2 wholes have 4 + 4 = 8.

q.t: 6/2 is how many wholes?
q.e: 2 halves make a whole, and 6 halves make 3 such wholes.

q.t: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices and Raju eats 3. What fraction did he eat?
q.e: The bottom counts all 8 equal slices; the top counts the 3 he ate.

q.t: In the fraction 3/7, what does the 7 tell us?
o: How many equal parts the whole is cut into
q.e: The bottom number counts the equal pieces in the whole; the top counts the pieces you have.
5 × 2 = 10, so multiply the top by 2 as well: 2 × 2 = 4.
3 × 4 = 12 on top, so the bottom is 4 × 4 = 16.

q.t: Which fraction is NOT equal to 1/3?
q.e: 2/6, 3/9 and 4/12 are 1/3 with top and bottom multiplied by the same number. 2/4 is equal to 1/2.

q.t: Which is the biggest: 3/7, 3/5, 3/10, 3/8?
q.e: Same top number: the smallest bottom means the biggest pieces.

q.t: Which is the smallest: 5/9, 2/9, 7/9, 4/9?
q.e: Same bottom number: the pieces are the same size, so fewest pieces is smallest.

q.t: Write 9/4 as wholes and a part.
q.e: 4 quarters make a whole. 9 = 4 + 4 + 1, so 2 wholes and 1 quarter.

q.t: 7 half-parathas make how many parathas?
q.e: 6 halves make 3 parathas, and 1 half is left over.

q.t: Are 6/9 and 2/3 equivalent?
o: Yes — divide top and bottom of 6/9 by 3
No — you must add 4 to get 6
Yes — take 4 away from top and bottom
q.e: 6 ÷ 3 = 2 and 9 ÷ 3 = 3, so 6/9 is just 2/3 cut into smaller pieces.
2 × 50 = 100, so multiply the top by 50 too: 1 × 50 = 50.

q.t: Sevi ate 4/6 of a paratha and Shami ate 4/5 of a same-size paratha. Who ate more?
q.e: Both ate 4 pieces, but fifths are bigger than sixths, so Shami’s 4 pieces were more.
2 × 3 = 6 on top, so the bottom is 5 × 3 = 15.

q.t: Which pair of fractions is equivalent?
q.e: 3 × 4 = 12 and 5 × 4 = 20, so 12/20 is 3/5 with each piece cut into 4.

q.t: Tamanna says 1/3 of her big chocolate is more than 1/2 of her small chocolate. Can she be right?
o: Yes — the two wholes are different sizes
q.e: A fraction is a share of something. We can only compare fractions of the SAME whole.

q.t: Maa takes 5 pieces, each 1/4 of a roti. How many rotis is that?
q.e: 4 quarters make 1 roti, and 1 quarter is left: 1 1/4.

q.t: How many 1/3 pieces make 2 whole chikkis?
q.e: Each chikki gives 3 thirds, so 2 chikkis give 3 + 3 = 6.

q.t: Which fraction is greater than 1?
q.e: When the top is bigger than the bottom, you have more pieces than make one whole.

q.t: 11/4 lies between which two whole numbers?
q.e: 8 quarters make 2 and 12 quarters make 3; 11 quarters is in between.

q.t: Raju says 1/3 = 2/4 because he added 1 to the top and the bottom. Is he right?
o: No — you must multiply top and bottom by the same number
Yes — adding the same number is fine
q.e: Adding changes the share. 1/3 = 2/6 (both × 2), but 2/4 = 1/2, which is bigger than 1/3.

q.t: A ribbon is cut into 8 equal parts. 3 parts are red, 4 parts are blue and the rest are yellow. What fraction is yellow?
q.e: 3 + 4 = 7 parts are red or blue, so 8 − 7 = 1 part out of 8 is yellow.

q.t: On a number line marked in halves starting at 0, what is the 7th mark after 0?
q.e: Each mark is 1/2 more. 7 halves = 3 wholes and 1 half.

q.t: A cake is cut into 12 equal parts. Asha eats 1/4 of the cake. How many parts does she eat?
q.e: 1/4 = 3/12, because 4 × 3 = 12 — so 1 quarter is 3 of the twelfths.

q.t: Mohan eats 2/6 of a pizza and Leela eats 1/3 of a same-size pizza. Who ate more?
q.e: 2/6 = 1/3 (divide top and bottom by 2), so they ate the same share.

q.t: Put 2/3, 2/5, 2/9 in order from smallest. Which is in the MIDDLE?
q.e: Same top number: the bigger the bottom, the smaller the pieces. 2/9 < 2/5 < 2/3.

q.t: 5 cakes are shared equally among 20 children. What fraction of a cake does each child get?
q.e: Each cake is cut into 4 equal parts to make 20 pieces in all, so each child gets 1/4.

q.t: 9 ribbon pieces, each 1/2 m long, are joined end to end. How long is the ribbon?
q.e: 2 halves make 1 m, so 9 halves = 4 m and 1 half left.

q.t: A full tank of water fills 4 buckets. How many buckets do 2 3/4 tanks fill?
q.e: 2 tanks fill 8 buckets, and 3/4 of a tank fills 3 buckets: 8 + 3 = 11.

q.t: Which fraction lies between 1/2 and 1?
q.e: 1/2 = 2/4, and 3/4 is one more quarter but still less than 4/4 = 1.
3 × 5 = 15 on top, so the bottom is 4 × 5 = 20.

q.t: Ravi cuts a chapati into 6 equal pieces and eats 3. Sita cuts a same-size chapati into 4 equal pieces and eats 2. Who ate more?
q.e: 3/6 and 2/4 are both equal to 1/2 — each ate half a chapati.

q.t: How many 1/4 kg packets are needed to make 3 kg?
q.e: 4 quarter-kg packets make 1 kg, so 3 kg needs 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.
